items.title: Buddy DeFranco interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: And according to Dave Mackey, who was the executor for the Glenn Miller estate

ctx.x: I guess it took him a while to find his sound but once he found it he really took it and ran with it.

Well actually it didn’t take him that long. I would go through the annals and the files of the Glenn Miller offices, and the archives, and I’d read scores of Glenn. Actually “Moonlight Serenade” was not “Moonlight Serenade” when he wrote it. He wrote it, he called it “Glenn’s Theme” and he wrote it as a graduation piece for Schillinger orchestration method and that was it. It was that lead clarinet with the saxes. And according to Dave Mackey, who was the executor for the Glenn Miller estate, he tried to sell…
We should pair that guy with the people who turned down the Beatles I guess.
